cards.explanation: The answer is His disciples and a large crowd. Luke says, "His disciples went with Him, accompanied by a large crowd." (Luke 7:11) So Jesus isn't walking alone. That's a whole parade heading toward Nain. I walk with a crowd only when somebody smells a fresh batch.

The answer is only. Luke says he is "…the only son of his mother…" (Luke 7:12) That's one son, and he's the one being carried out. I think that makes the scene even heavier. This is a hard moment, friends, and Luke doesn't rush past it.

The answer is False. Luke says the dead man was "…the only son of his mother, and she was a widow." (Luke 7:12) A widow's husband has died. So she has no husband, and her only son is the one being carried out. I think this is a heavy part of the story.
The answer is compassion. Luke says, "When the Lord saw her, He had compassion on her…" (Luke 7:13) He sees her, and compassion is what He has for her. Friends, that's the whole tone of this scene.

The answer is "Do not weep." Jesus says to her, "Do not weep." (Luke 7:13) Those are His words to a mother in the middle of a funeral. Think about that for a second, bakers. A line like that could sound empty from anyone else, but the story is about to show who's saying it.

The answer is False. The men carrying the coffin don't keep walking. Luke says, "Then He went up and touched the coffin, and those carrying it stood still." (Luke 7:14) They stand still, friends. I bet they had no idea what was coming next.

The answer is the young man in the coffin. Jesus says, "Young man, I tell you, get up!" (Luke 7:14) He speaks right to the one in the coffin. I would have talked to the mourners. Jesus talks to the young man.

The answer is True. Luke says, "…the dead man sat up and began to speak!" (Luke 7:15) Jesus speaks, and the young man sits up. He doesn't just sit up, friends, he starts talking. I'd love to know what a first word like that sounds like, but the text doesn't tell us.

The answer is mother. Luke says, "Then Jesus gave him back to his mother." (Luke 7:15) She's the widow from verse 12, and he's her only son. I think that's the moment the whole story has been heading toward.

The answer is a sense of awe. Luke says, "A sense of awe swept over all of them, and they glorified God." (Luke 7:16) Awe is that stunned feeling you get when something is bigger than you. It swept over all of them, not just a few. I think their mouths were hanging open.

The answer is prophet. The people say, "A great prophet has appeared among us!" (Luke 7:16) A prophet is someone who speaks for God. That's what the people say when they see this happen, friends. They also say, "God has visited His people!"

The answer is False. The news doesn't stay in Nain. Luke says, "…the news about Jesus spread throughout Judea and all the surrounding region." (Luke 7:17) The news goes throughout Judea and the region around it. That's way past the town gate.
